text:
Maria: Quick heads-up — we need to lock the fallback compatibility matrix for smart routing by tier/region. Running into edge cases where a model variant differs in tokenizer and tool-calling.
Sam: Are we planning to allow automatic fallback to variants that don't support tool-calls?
Lee: short answer: no by default. Tool-calling parity is a hard requirement for any transparent fallback. Otherwise we risk silent failures in workflows that expect tools.
Olivia: Product wants a softer degrade path for lower tiers — e.g., fallback to non-tool variant but surface a structured 422 + metadata so app can decide. Can we support that? :thinking_face:
Maria: That could work if we require explicit opt-in per customer and per route. Also need to annotate console rollout UX for visibility (per-route indicators).
Sam: Practically, that means our compatibility matrix needs columns: tokenizer_compat, context_len_min, max_context_preserve, tool_call_parity, and signal_type (silent/fail/soft-degrade).
Lee: Agreed. Proposed minimal matrix snippet: ```
variant, tokenizer_compat, ctx_len, tool_call_parity, recommended_action
redwood-7b-v1, yes, 4096, partial, surface-warning
redwood-7b-q4, no, 2048, no, block-fallback
opt-7b-tool, yes, 8192, yes, allow-fallback
```
Olivia: For rollout UX, can we show: "Fallback allowed: yes/no (reason)" and a quick link to test prompts that exercise tool-calls? That'll help PMs sign off.
Maria: Telemetry question: when a fallback occurs, we should emit an event with fields [original_model, fallback_model, route, customer_tier, truncated_tokens, tools_invoked_expected, tools_invoked_actual]. That lets SRE + product measure regressions.
Sam: Also need a rule for context length mismatch: if fallback has shorter ctx, should we reject requests that exceed fallback ctx or auto-truncate? Auto-truncation makes debugging messy.
Lee: Prefer reject with a detailed error with suggestion: "pin to original model" or "enable explicit soft-degrade". We can add a helper SDK error enum for this: FallbackRejected_ContextTooLong.
Olivia: Can we add an A/B canary where 10% of traffic returns soft-degrade with annotated metadata and 0 side effects? Product wants to monitor quality impact.
Maria: Yes — rollout config should include canary_pct and telemetry_mode (sampled/verbose). Add UX checkbox for "Enable soft-degrade canary".
Sam: Implementation notes: router needs to consult compatibility matrix at decision time. Matrix must be versioned and pinned to rollout so changes are auditable.
Lee: We'll need an authoring UI for matrix edits and a dry-run mode that logs hypothetical fallback decisions.
DeployBot: deploy:compat-matrix-service v0.6.1 queued for staging at 2026-03-18T15:20:00Z :rocket:
Maria: Action items: 1) Lee — prototype compatibility schema and dry-run API (this week). 2) Sam — add error enums + SDK behavior doc. 3) Olivia — define product acceptance criteria for soft-degrade. 4) Maria — add console mockups for per-route fallback indicators.
Sam: tiny follow-up: do we want tokenizer_compat to be boolean or a compatibility score? Some variants are byte-level compatible but differ subtly.
Lee: start boolean + notes field. If we need granularity later, we can add scores.
Olivia: Thanks all. Leaving this thread for the design doc link when available. :+1:
